quote: Well, I got home work today to find my 13.5 month old son holding 2 positive pregnancy tests. I am stunned.
cx: A father learns of an unplanned second pregnancy.

quote: I just started a new job less than a month ago and big selling point if the new job was I’d get 4 weeks paternity leave, but I just read that you aren’t eligible until you’ve worked there for at least 12 months. I had 6 weeks at my last job when we had our first and it was an incredible blessing.
cx: The leave he took the job for will not apply to this birth.

quote: So I just know when I tell my wife I won’t be eligible for paternity leave it’s going to be 10x more devastating for her. She left her job after her first to be home which has also been much more difficult than we anticipated so the thought of her home alone with 2 under 2 during the day is not an easy thought.
cx: Same father on telling his wife there will be no paternity leave.

quote: She also started recently calling my baby "our baby," which makes me really uncomfortable. The first time she said it, I assumed she misspoke, but she’s continued saying it.
cx: Nearly 12 weeks, first child; her adoptive mother's excitement crosses lines.

quote: She also sends me Facebook reels all day long. Usually anywhere from 3–20 a day. […] One was a video titled something like, "Why does your toddler always want Grandma over you? A child psychologist explains." **OMG.**
cx: The videos her mother sends her in the first trimester.

quote: I also have no idea how me and my partner will split time with every grandparent wanting to see our child and having all of these expectations like having equipment at their house and expecting visits and such. **I AM OVERWHELMED.**
cx: Planning grandparent access before the end of the first trimester.

quote: My dad also posted a picture of my ultrasound on Facebook. That's how my biological mother found out I was pregnant, even though right before the ultrasound I had been telling my parents I wasn't ready to tell that side of my family yet
cx: How news of the pregnancy got out before she was ready.

quote: It is laughable how much of this pregnancy I have spent managing other people's feelings and expectations about my unborn baby's foreskin.
cx: Her parents and mother-in-law have pushed back for months on a family decision about the baby.

quote: Now she mentioned getting a changing table. I said she didn't need to get a changing table since I have a portable changing pad and she said "well if I have to change him I can't bend down," and I laughed and said there's no world in which she is changing him
cx: Her mother planning to babysit after months of conflict.

quote: We had planned on waiting at least another year - so it's all a bit overwhelming right now. I feel like I'm mourning the plan we had. I don't feel ready to share my attention with my daughter and another baby. I like being her world and her being ours.
cx: A father of an 11-month-old the day of a surprise positive test.

quote: Just seeing this now along with a few other positive messages after deleting it due to the hateful comments.
cx: He deleted his post after replies attacked him.

quote: So I made the call to move the party to avoid drama, she said she wasn’t going to go but my dad said he would of course come for me and my baby. Guess what? That was a lie.
cx: 32 weeks, two days before her shower; her father's wife objected to the venue.

quote: I want my mom to come stay with us for about a month after the baby is born. My MIL also wants to come for a month+. […] my husband really wants both of our moms staying in our house together. He thinks it would be beautiful to have everyone there and that they'd both be helpful.
cx: First baby due in December; the couple disagree on who stays for the first month.

quote: The bigger issue is that I know my mom will actually be there to help and won't make me feel judged. My MIL is a different story.
cx: Why she wants one grandmother and not both.

quote: I suggested his mom come a month later, but she wants to be here for the birth and Christmas, so that's off the table.
cx: Timing the mother-in-law's long stay around the December birth.

quote: At the same time, I'm the one recovering from childbirth, and going through one of the most vulnerable periods of my life. I can't help but feel like my comfort should carry a little more weight during those first few weeks.
cx: Her case to her husband.

quote:
Hosting is work! Even with easy guests. He may not consciously think about meals, bathrooms, towels, whether everyone is comfortable or is anyone feeling left out, but I do.

Even if they help with the house load, what about my mental and emotional load?
cx: Why house guests after the birth are not simply help.

quote:
I have to remind him every single day to talk to my tummy so the baby gets used to his voice. He never just does it naturally.

If we need something for our baby, I have to send him exact links and tell him to buy it.
cx: 36 weeks after years of trying; her husband dotes on his niece and nephew.

quote: The other day, I was praising how amazing my sister has been, and his sister said, "Oh, he's so lucky he's going to have the best aunt in the world," completely ignoring the fact that she is also going to be his aunt.
cx: Her sister-in-law has barely acknowledged the pregnancy.

quote: Is it normal for guys to just not "get it" until the baby is physically here?
cx: Same post, what she asks strangers.

quote: So I accidentally found out that my boyfriend and his mum are planning a surprise baby shower for me. Baby showers are realllyyyy not my thing […] I can’t help but selfishly feel frustrated because I feel like I’m not being heard
cx: Heavily pregnant in the UK; she has told everyone she doesn't want a shower.

quote: She’s freaking out because we can’t find a picture of it online and doesn’t want to talk about it anymore at DR’s office, please someone help me comfort her with a story about how this happened to another woman.
cx: A husband at 37 weeks asks for one similar story after the midwife called a change normal.
